info.title: RBAC_Rule_Entry
info.description: RESTful interface for AOS-CX switch software

action.description: 'permit': User operation will be allowed. 'deny':   User operation will be denied. RBAC rule will only be activated when an associated action is provided. If `action` is not provided, the RBAC rule will be ignored as only comment is provided.

cli.description: If `command` is not provided, the RBAC rule will be ignored  during the authorization of the CLI commands.

command.description: POSIX compliant regular expression that matches  one or more CLI commands.

comment.description: Comment associated with the RBAC rule. If not set, there is no comment associated to the RBAC rule and only action is set.

invalid_reason.description: Indicates the reason why the RBAC rule is invalid. Empty when  the RBAC rule is `valid` or `not_processed`. 'missing_action'           : The `action` field is missing. 'missing_regex'            : The `command` regex in `cli` field is missing. 'invalid_cli_command_regex': The `command` regex in `cli` field is invalid.

sequence_number.description:
Reference Resource: [RBAC_Rule_Entry](#/RBAC_Rule_Entry)
Role Based Access Control rules applicable to a user group. When local authorization is added to AAA authorization list, these rules will be traversed in an ascending order of the sequence number to find a rule that matches the user operation on the switch. The matching rule determines whether the user operation is allowed or denied. If no rule matches, user operation will be denied.

status.description: Indicates the status of the RBAC rule. Only the valid RBAC rules  are used during local authorization. 'valid'        : An RBAC rule is valid if one of the conditions are met.                  - Only `comment` is provided.                  - `action` and `cli` are provided with a valid                      POSIX compliant `command` regex.                  - `comment`, `action` and `cli` are provided with a                      valid POSIX compliant `command` regex. 'invalid'      : The RBAC rule is invalid. 'not_processed': The RBAC rule is not processed yet.

parameters.name: User_Group.name
parameters.description:
Reference Resource: [User_Group](#/User_Group)
Name of the user group. Built-in user groups are as follows: `administrators`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 15. Members have access to: All the CLI commands and bash shell. All the REST Methods through REST APIs. `operators`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 1. Members have access to: All "show" CLI commands (except those that display sensitive information). All "GET" requests through REST APIs. `auditors`: System-defined group with associated privilege level of 19. Members have access to: All "show" CLI commands to display and copy security logs. All "GET" requests for security logs through REST APIs. Only users belonging to the above three default groups will be allowed access to REST APIs.

parameters.name: attributes
parameters.description: Columns to display.

parameters.name: depth
parameters.description: Depth to traverse.

parameters.name: selector
parameters.description: Select configuration, status and/or statistics. Default is all categories.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Filter rows by attribute values.  Format: attribute:value

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Count the number of rows found.

parameters.name: If-None-Match
parameters.description: Entity-tag value for representation comparison (see RFC 7232 - Conditional Requests - section 3.2)
